newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIA ASIAN SEES 97/98 SALES UP 15 PCT.
newsitem.headline: INDIA ASIAN SEES 97/98 SALES UP 15 PCT.

text.p: India's leading paint manufacturer, Asian Paints expects 15 percent sales growth in 1997/98 (April-March), a senior official said at the firm's annual general meeting.
"There are early signs of a recovery in the demand for paints and I am cautiously optimistic," Ashwin Choksey told share holders on Friday.
The firm said first quarter sales from its paints division grew nine percent in the period ending June 30, 1997.

"Our growth over the years has been achieved though a series of measured steps. Our investments in facilities, people and systems have enabled us to build on our capabilities and opened up new opportunites at every step," Choksey said.
"Stimulating continuous progress while at the same time, preserving our core beliefs and values is the task we have set ourselves," the acting chairman told shareholders.
The fifth paints manufacturing plant with a total capacity of 25,000 tonnes will be set up in Mahad in the state of Maharashtra, Choksey said in a reply to shareholder queries.
The firm plans a total investment of about one billion rupees in the project, Choksey added.
